cards.explanation: The answer is wailing. Verse 30 says there was loud wailing in Egypt, "for there was no house without someone dead." I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story, friends, and it's okay to let it be heavy for a moment. The sound that night was grief, spreading through the whole land.

The answer is that Pharaoh tells them to get up and leave. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, tells Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, his brother (Exodus 4:14), "Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested." Back in Exodus 5:2 he said he would not let Israel go. I think he was done bargaining, friends. Now he's the one doing the pushing.

The answer is True. Verse 32 has Pharaoh saying, "Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart!" That's a big change, friends. Earlier he told them that their flocks and herds had to stay behind (Exodus 10:24). Now the animals are going too.

The answer is that he asks them to bless him too. He ends with, "And bless me also." (Exodus 12:32) Think about that, friends. Back in Exodus 5:2 Pharaoh said, "I do not know the LORD," and now he's asking Moses and Aaron for a blessing as he sends them off. That's quite a turn.

The answer is die. The Egyptians urge the people on and say, "For otherwise… we are all going to die!" (Exodus 12:33) After a night like that, I think they were scared. They weren't waiting around for a second invitation, friends. Imagine somebody holding the door open and pointing.

The answer is in kneading bowls on their shoulders. Verse 34 says the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing. My mustache handles cookie boxes all day, but a whole bowl of dough? I'd have dough all over my chef's hat. These folks were on the move, friends.

The answer is False. The Israelites asked for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing, and the Egyptians said yes (Exodus 12:35-36). The text says, "In this way they plundered the Egyptians." That's the opposite of being turned down, friends.

The answer is that the LORD gave the people favor with them. Verse 36 says, "…the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request." The Egyptians weren't pushed into it by a clever sales pitch, friends. The LORD gave the favor, and that's the whole reason.

The answer is Succoth. Verse 37 says the Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth. The text adds that there were about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children. That's a LOT of people on the move, friends, and I bet somebody in that crowd was already wondering if they were there yet.

The answer is about six hundred thousand. The text says about 600,000 men on foot, "…besides women and children." (Exodus 12:37) Count the women and children too, friends, and it's even bigger. I'd need a LOT of cookie boxes just to say hello to this crowd.

The answer is False. Verse 38 says, "…a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds." So not everyone on that road was an Israelite, friends. The text doesn't say more about who they were. It just says they went up too.

The answer is False. The text says the people "…had not prepared any provisions for themselves." (Exodus 12:39) Their dough had no leaven, so they baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. I've scrambled to finish a batch before the timer, friends, but never with a deadline like this.

The answer is that they were driven out and couldn't delay. Verse 39 says, "For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay…" Think about the morning you're running late and you leave with one shoe and half a plan. Now make that a whole nation. I've baked under pressure, friends, but nobody handed me a deadline like that. The rush is why the provisions never got prepared.

The answer is True. Verse 41 says, "At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt." To the very day, friends. After 430 years, the text still counts the day.

The answer is all the Israelites, for generations to come. Verse 42 says this same night "…is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come." It's not a night for a few, friends. It's for everyone, and it keeps going down the generations.

The answer is True. Verse 50 says, "Then all the Israelites did this—they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron." Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, his brother (Exodus 4:14), were the ones who received the command. The people did just what He said, friends.
